facts.statement: The genus Tupandactylus was established by Kellner and Campos in 2007.
facts.quote: authority: Kellner & Campos, 2007

facts.statement: The species T. imperator was originally described by Campos and Kellner in 1997 as a species of Tapejara.
facts.quote: T. imperator was described in 1997 by D. A. Campos and Alexander W. A. Kellner, who assigned it to Tapejara.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, a skull and partial lower jaw, was found in the Crato Formation and dates to about 112 million years ago at the Aptian-Albian boundary.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of Tupandactylus is MCT 1622-R, a skull and partial lower jaw, found in the Crato Formation, dating to the boundary of the Aptian-Albian stages of the early Cretaceous period, about 112 Ma ago.

facts.statement: A 2021 study suggested that T. imperator and T. navigans might be different sexes of a single sexually dimorphic species, though this requires further testing.
facts.quote: A 2021 study describing a very complete T. navigans specimen suggested that the two species might represent different sexes of one sexually dimorphic species, but cautioned that further study was needed to test this.

facts.statement: Tupandactylus is a genus of tapejarid pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous Crato Formation of Brazil.
facts.quote: Tupandactylus (meaning "Tupâ or Tupan finger", in reference to a personification of the Tupi supreme deity) is a genus of tapejarid pterodactyloid pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous Crato Formation of Brazil.

facts.statement: T. imperator had a large, rounded crest, while T. navigans had a tall, vertical crest.
facts.quote: T. imperator, the crest was large and rounded, whereas in T. navigans, it was tall and vertical.

facts.statement: Tupandactylus is notable for a large cranial crest made of both bone and soft tissue fibers, likely keratin.
facts.quote: Tupandactylus is notable for its large cranial crest, composed partly of bone and partly of soft tissue fibres, likely keratin.

facts.statement: Rhamphotheca, or beaks, are known from multiple Tupandactylus specimens.
facts.quote: Rhamphotheca are known from multiple Tupandactylus specimens.

facts.statement: The lower jaw had a slightly downturned symphysis and was also crested like the skull.
facts.quote: The dentary had a mandibular symphysis which was slightly downturned towards the front. Like the skull, the dentary was crested.

facts.statement: The first five dorsal vertebrae of Tupandactylus are fused into a notarium, a structure also found in some other pterosaurs and birds.
facts.quote: The first five dorsal (back) vertebrae are fused into a notarium, like in some other pterosaurs and birds, and particularly ornithocheiroids.

facts.statement: The genus Tupandactylus includes the species T. imperator and T. navigans.
facts.quote: subdivision: Tupandactylus imperator(Campos & Kellner, 1997) Tupandactylus navigans(Frey, Martill & Buchy, 2003)

facts.statement: While two species are currently recognized, it has been suggested that there may be only a single, highly sexually dimorphic species.
facts.quote: It is known from two species, T. imperator and T. navigans, though it has been suggested that there is only a single, highly sexually dimorphic species (which would then be T. imperator).

facts.statement: There was a taxonomic debate where Unwin and Martill proposed the genus name "Ingridia" for both species, but Campos and Kellner's proposed name "Tupandactylus" was ultimately accepted because their publication preceded the book by Unwin and Martill.
facts.quote: One, by David Unwin and David Martill, would have seen them both assigned to the new genus "Ingridia"; the other, by Campos and Kellner, erected the genus Tupandactylus; ultimately, the latter name was used, since the publication by Unwin and Martill was published in a book months after the competing study.

facts.statement: The sternum of Tupandactylus was wide and roughly square.
facts.quote: The sternum of Tupandactylus was wide and roughly square.

facts.statement: The radius and ulna of Tupandactylus were straight and lightly built.
facts.quote: The radius and ulna, the two bones of the forearm, were straight and lightly built.

facts.statement: A well-preserved fossil of T. imperator had pigment cells with forms similar to modern birds, more complex than those previously known from other pterosaurs.
facts.quote: A well preserved fossil of T. imperator was found to have pigment cells with similar forms to those seen in modern birds, more complex in organization than those previously known from other pterosaurs.

facts.statement: A specimen of T. imperator suggests the presence of Stage IIIa feathers, indicating complex filament structures in pterosaurs.
facts.quote: This specimen also suggest the presence of Stage IIIa feathers, further indication of more complex filament structures in pterosaurs.

facts.statement: Tupandactylus is distinguished by its large cranial crest, composed partly of bone and partly of soft tissue.
facts.quote: Destaca por su gran cresta craneal, compuesta en parte de hueso y en parte de tejido blando.

facts.statement: The crests of Tupandactylus consisted of a semicircular crest over the snout, and in the type species T. imperator, a bony spike extending backward behind the head.
facts.quote: Las crestas de Tupandactylus consistían en una cresta semicircular sobre el hocico y, en el caso de la especie tipo T. imperator, una púa ósea que se extendía hacia atrás detrás de la cabeza.

facts.statement: The second species, T. navigans, lacked this spike and had a much more vertical crest.
facts.quote: Una segunda especie, T. navigans, carecía de esta púa y tenía una cresta mucho más vertical.

facts.statement: Soft tissue impressions show that the small bony crests were extended by a much larger structure made of keratinous material.
facts.quote: Las impresiones de tejidos blandos también muestran que las pequeñas crestas óseas estaban extendidas por una estructura mucho más grande hecha de material queratinoso.

facts.statement: The complete crest of T. navigans rose into a sharp "dome," resembling a sail, well above the rest of the skull.
facts.quote: La cresta completa de T. navigans se elevó en una "cúpula" afilada, parecida a una vela, muy por encima del resto del cráneo.

facts.statement: Tupandactylus is based on material MCT 1622-R, an almost complete skull found in the Santana Formation.
facts.quote: Tupandactylus se basa en el material de MCT 1622-R, un cráneo casi completo, encontrado en la Formación Santana.

facts.statement: It was initially described as a species of Tapejara, but later research indicated it was a separate genus.
facts.quote: Fue descrito inicialmente como una especie de Tapejara, pero la investigación posterior indicó que era un género aparte.

facts.statement: Tupandactylus lived during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Cretácico Inferior

facts.statement: Tupandactylus is a pterodactyloid tapejarid pterosaur genus from the Early Cretaceous Crato Formation of Brazil.
facts.quote: es un género de pterosaurio pterodactiloide tapejarido de la Formación Crato del Cretácico Inferior de Brasil.

facts.statement: Examination of specimen GP/2E 9266 suggests Tupandactylus was capable of flight but spent much time on the ground due to its large crest, long forelimbs, and long neck, taking only short flights possibly to escape predators.
facts.quote: Examination of the specimen GP/2E 9266 suggests that the pterosaur was capable of flight, but seemingly spent much of its time on the ground thanks to its large crest, longer forelimbs, and a relatively long neck, only taking short flights to possibly escape from predators.

facts.statement: The mandible of the well-preserved T. imperator skull is associated with plant material, which may represent a taphonomic phenomenon or tentative evidence of herbivory.
facts.quote: The mandible portion of the well-preserved T. imperator skull is directly associated with plant material, either representing a taphonomic phenomenon or possibly a tentative evidence of herbivory.

facts.statement: The common origin of pterosaur feathers and bird feathers remains controversial.
facts.quote: This common origin had been suggested before, but remains controversial.

facts.statement: Frey, Martill, and Buchy argued in 2003 that the large head crest significantly impacted aerodynamics and that adaptations to counteract it were absent.
facts.quote: In their 2003 paper describing T. navigans, Eberhard Frey, David Martill, and Marie-Céline Buchy argued that it would have significantly impacted its aerodynamics, and that adaptations to counteract it (i.e. a reduced neck with tendon locks on each cervical vertebra) were conspicuously absent.

facts.statement: Both T. navigans and T. imperator are found within the tribe Tapejarini, which is within the larger group Tapejaridae.
facts.quote: They found both T. navigans and T. imperator within the tribe Tapejarini, which in turn was within the larger group Tapejaridae.

facts.statement: The genus Tupandactylus was named by Kellner and Campos in 2007.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Kellner & Campos, 2007

facts.statement: Ingridia is a synonym of Tupandactylus, proposed by Unwin and Martill in 2007.
facts.quote: synonyms: Ingridia Unwin & Martill, 2007

facts.statement: Researchers Kellner and Campos proposed the new genus Tupandactylus in 2006 because they found that species previously assigned to Tapejara were anatomically distinct.
facts.quote: En 2006, varios investigadores, incluyendo Kellner y Campos (quienes nombraron a Tupandactylus), habían encontrado que las tres especies asignadas tradicionalmente al género Tapejara ( T. wellnhofferi, T. imperator y T. navigans) son de hecho distintas en anatomía y en sus relaciones con otros pterosaurios, y necesitaban un nuevo nombre genérico.

facts.statement: The species T. navigans was formally reclassified into the genus Tupandactylus in 2011.
facts.quote: No fue hasta 2011 que T. navigans fue reclasificado formalmente en el género Tupandactylus, en un estudio subsecuente que apoyaba las conclusiones de Unwin y Martill en 2007.

facts.statement: The genus Ingridia is considered a junior synonym of Tupandactylus.
facts.quote: Por lo tanto Ingridia se considera un sinónimo más moderno de Tupandactylus.

facts.statement: Tupandactylus belongs to the parent group Tapejaridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Tapejaridae

facts.statement: Tupandactylus is classified within the family Tapejaridae.
facts.quote: Family: Tapejaridae

facts.statement: Tupandactylus is classified as a reptile.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Tupandactylus lived during the Aptian stage, between 119.57 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (119.57 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: A research team suggested that the thin crest on Tupandactylus's head acted as a sensory organ similar to a modern flight computer to help control agility.
facts.quote: La gran cresta delgada en su cabeza a modo de vela serviría como un órgano sensorial que actuaría de manera similar a una computadora de vuelo en una aeronave moderna y también ayudaría a controlar su agilidad para girar.

facts.statement: Researchers proposed that Tupandactylus could use its wings like boat sails to catch light breezes and move like a catamaran.
facts.quote: Al alzar sus alas como las velas de un bote, pudieron usar la más leve brisa de la misma manera en que un catamarán se mueve por el agua.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Tupandactylus could sail using its wings, as some studies suggest tapejarids had short wings adapted for terrestrial life and climbing trees rather than sailing.
facts.quote: No obstante, la precisión de estos estudios ha sido puesta en duda. Se ha señalado que los tapejáridos tenían alas cortas, tan dotadas para el planeo como las de las aves Galliformes, las cuales son más coherentes con adaptaciones para la vida terrestre y trepar a los árboles.

facts.statement: There is no evidence supporting an aerodynamic function for the crest, and some researchers argue that the original proponent of this idea ignored recent aerodynamic studies.
facts.quote: Igualmente, no se ha percibido evidencia de una función aerodinámica de la cresta, y Sankar Chatterjee parece haber ignorado los más recientes estudios aerodinámicos sobre los pterosaurios para sus conclusiones.

facts.statement: The species T. navigans appeared in the 1999 TV series Walking with Dinosaurs, but it was not formally described and named until 2003.
facts.quote: Curiosamente, aunque la serie fue estrenada en 1999, T. navigans no fue formalmente descrito y nombrado hasta 2003.
